messages.subject: space-varying regression coefficients
parts:
Hi,

I'd like to fit a model with space-varying regression coefficients, much like example 4 (slide 54) here: http://www.rni.helsinki.fi/~jmh/mrf08/R-INLA.pdf

The model specification for the latent regression parameters given in that example (using the weights argument of f() to supply covariate values) seems to be no longer supported and I cannot deduce the equivalent model specification with the current INLA version. Any help you can offer is much appreciated!

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] space-varying regression coefficients
parts:
Hi Dan,
I'm not sure quite what you mean.  Here's an example that runs on the current (testing) version of INLA

It fits the a disease mapping model with a spatially varying covariate (the third f in the formula), a sturctured spatial effect (the besag model) and an i.i.d. model comonent.


library(INLA)
data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
Germany$region.struct = Germany$region

Germany$region.x = Germany$region

formula4 = Y ~ f(region.struct, model="besag", graph=g) +
               f(region,model="iid") +
               f(region.x, x, model = "besag",
                 graph=g, constr=FALSE)

result4 = inla(formula4, family="poisson", data=Germany, E=E,
   control.compute= list(mlik=TRUE,dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

Best wishes,

D

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] space-varying regression coefficients
parts:
Just to point out one of the notational quirks here (sorry Håvard), weights is not a valid argument for f().  

The first argument is un-named (denoted ... in the help) and it is usually just the name of the effect, i.e. f(<name of covariate>, model= .....).  

In the case where there are weights, the un-named argument has the name and the weights and the call is  f(<name of covariate>, <weights>, model=.....)

Hope this clears it up.

Dan

On 16 April 2014 08:10, Zhao Xing <zhaox...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Would you explain what does the argument 'constr=F' mean here?, and why do
> we need it?

I'm not Daniel, but the documentation provides partial answers to the
original thread question as well as this one. The syntax appears to
have changes since the linked example was written (it has weights as a
later named argument in a different position):

> ?f
...: Name of the covariate and, possibly of the weights vector.
NB: order counts!!!! The first specified term is the
covariate and the second one is the vector of weights.
constr: A boolean variable indicating whater to set a sum to 0
constraint on the term. By default the sum to 0 constraint is
imposed on all intrinsic models ("iid","rw1","rw1","besag",
etc..).

I'm not sure why the constraint is disabled in Daniel's example.
One common thing would be to disable the model intercept instead
of enforcing the sum-to-zero-constraint, but the example _has_ an intercept).

Finn

parts: It means the component is not constrained to sum to zero.  The constraint is the default behaviour and makes sense in a lot of situations, but for the coefficient of a coefficient it's nonsense: you'd be forcing the covariate to have, on average, zero effect.
